pairs.source_text: C. Plinius Traiano imperatori. Tua quidem pietas, imperator sanctissime, optaverat, ut quam tardissime succederes patri; sed di immortales festinaverunt virtutes tuas ad gubernacula rei publicae quam susceperas admovere.
pairs.question: Ad quem imperatorem Plinius minor epistulas decimi libri suas direxit, a quo vicissim responsa accepit?
pairs.question_en: To which emperor did Pliny the Younger address his letters of the tenth book, and from whom he received replies in turn?
pairs.derivation: Addressee fact: the whole of Book X is the official correspondence between Pliny and the emperor Trajan; the salutations read 'C. Plinius Traiano imperatori' / 'Traianus Plinio', and 10.1 addresses Trajan as the new emperor who succeeded his (adoptive) father Nerva. Closed-book famous; entity-anchored to Pliny + Book X; single-name answer.

pairs.source_text: Rursus, cum transissem in orarias nauculas, contrariis ventis retentus aliquanto tardius quam speraveram, id est XV Kal. Octobres, Bithyniam intravi.
pairs.question: In quam provinciam, a Traiano legatus missus, Plinius minor ante diem quintum decimum Kalendas Octobres ingressus est?
pairs.question_en: Into which province, sent as Trajan's legate, did Pliny the Younger enter on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of October (17 September)?
pairs.derivation: Province fact: Pliny governed the province of Bithynia (and Pontus) as Trajan's special legate; he records 'Bithyniam intravi' on a.d. XV Kal. Oct. Answer supported verbatim. Closed-book famous (Pliny's governorship of Bithynia). The full province was Bithynia et Pontus (cf. 10.108 'Bithynas et Ponticas civitates', 10.112 'Bithyni et Pontici').

pairs.source_text: Cognitionibus de Christianis interfui numquam: ideo nescio quid et quatenus aut puniri soleat aut quaeri.
pairs.question: Cuius generis hominum cognitionibus se numquam interfuisse Plinius minor Traiano scribens fatetur?
pairs.question_en: At the trials of what kind of people does Pliny the Younger, writing to Trajan, confess he had never been present?
pairs.derivation: The famous letter 10.96, in which Pliny consults Trajan on how to handle Christians, opens by admitting he had never attended cognitiones de Christianis. Entity-anchored (Pliny + Christians), short answer supported verbatim, closed-book famous.

pairs.source_text: Affirmabant autem hanc fuisse summam vel culpae suae vel erroris, quod essent soliti stato die ante lucem convenire, carmenque Christo quasi deo dicere secum invicem.
pairs.question: Cui Christiani, ut Plinio confessi sunt, stato die ante lucem coeuntes carmen quasi deo invicem dicere soliti erant?
pairs.question_en: To whom, as the Christians confessed to Pliny, were they accustomed to recite a hymn as to a god, gathering before dawn on a fixed day, in turn?
pairs.derivation: The celebrated description of early Christian worship: they met before dawn on a fixed day and sang 'carmen Christo quasi deo dicere secum invicem'. Entity-anchored (Christians, Christ), short name answer supported verbatim, closed-book famous.

pairs.source_text: Interrogavi ipsos an essent Christiani. Confitentes iterum ac tertio interrogavi supplicium minatus; perseverantes duci iussi.
pairs.question: Quid Plinius, supplicium minatus, de iis fieri iussit qui pertinaciter se Christianos esse confitebantur?
pairs.question_en: What did Pliny, having threatened punishment, order to be done to those who persistently confessed they were Christians?
pairs.answer_en: He ordered them led off (to execution).
pairs.derivation: Pliny's procedure: those who persisted in confessing (perseverantes) he ordered 'duci', i.e. led off to execution, holding that obstinacy must be punished. Entity-anchored (Pliny, Christians), short verbal answer supported verbatim.

pairs.source_text: Conquirendi non sunt; si deferantur et arguantur, puniendi sunt.
pairs.question: Quid Traianus, Plinio rescribens, de Christianis conquirendis statuit?
pairs.question_en: What did Trajan rule, in his reply to Pliny, about hunting out Christians?
pairs.answer_en: That they are not to be sought out.
pairs.derivation: Trajan's rescript (10.97), the first of its two famous rulings: Christians 'conquirendi non sunt' (they are not to be searched out, though they are to be punished if denounced and convicted). Entity-anchored (Trajan, Christians), short answer supported verbatim, closed-book famous.

pairs.source_text: Sine auctore vero propositi libelli in nullo crimine locum habere debent. Nam et pessimi exempli nec nostri saeculi est.
pairs.question: Quem locum Traianus libellis sine auctore propositis in criminibus tribuendum esse negavit?
pairs.answer: Nullum: in nullo crimine locum habere debent.
pairs.question_en: What standing did Trajan deny should be granted to anonymous written accusations in any charge?
pairs.answer_en: None: they are to have no place in any charge.
pairs.derivation: The second famous ruling of Trajan's rescript: anonymous denunciations ('sine auctore propositi libelli') are to have no place in any charge, being a bad precedent unworthy of the age. Entity-anchored (Trajan), short answer supported verbatim, closed-book famous.

pairs.source_text: Cautum est, domine, Pompeia lege quae Bithynis data est, ne quis capiat magistratum neve sit in senatu minor annorum triginta.
pairs.question: Minor quot annorum, ex lege Pompeia Bithynis data, magistratum capere aut in senatu esse non poterat?
pairs.question_en: Younger than how many years, by the lex Pompeia given to the Bithynians, could a man not hold a magistracy or sit in the senate?
pairs.derivation: Institutional fact: the lex Pompeia (Pompey's organization of Bithynia) barred anyone under thirty from holding local magistracy or sitting in the local senate. Entity-anchored (lex Pompeia, Bithynia), number answer supported verbatim ('minor annorum triginta').

pairs.source_text: Tu, domine, dispice an instituendum putes collegium fabrorum dumtaxat hominum CL.
pairs.question: Quod collegium Plinius, post vastissimum Nicomediae incendium, instituendum Traiano proposuit?
pairs.question_en: What guild did Pliny propose to Trajan should be established after a devastating fire at Nicomedia?
pairs.answer_en: A guild of workmen (a fire brigade, collegium fabrorum).
pairs.derivation: After a fire devastated Nicomedia, Pliny proposed establishing a collegium fabrorum (capped at 150 men) to fight fires; Trajan refused (10.34), fearing such associations would quickly become political clubs (hetaeriae). Entity-anchored (Pliny, Nicomedia), short answer; a recognizable exchange in the history of Roman associations.

pairs.source_text: Tuo tamen desiderio subscripsi et dedisse me ius trium liberorum Suetonio Tranquillo ea condicione, qua assuevi, referri in commentarios meos iussi.
pairs.question: Cui viro erudito, postea 'De vita Caesarum' auctori, Plinius a Traiano ius trium liberorum impetravit?
pairs.question_en: For which learned man, later author of the 'Lives of the Caesars', did Pliny obtain from Trajan the 'right of three children'?
pairs.derivation: Pliny was the patron of the biographer Suetonius and secured the ius trium liberorum for him from Trajan. Entity-anchored to Suetonius; single-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book: Suetonius's link to Pliny is well known; the descriptor 'author of De vita Caesarum' is a true external identifier.

pairs.source_text: In aquae ductum, domine, Nicomedenses impenderunt HS XXX CCCXVIII, qui imperfectus adhuc omissus, destructus etiam est; rursus in alium ductum erogata sunt CC.
pairs.question: Quae civitas, ut Plinius Traiano scribit, magnam pecuniam in aquae ductus imperfectos frustra erogaverat?
pairs.question_en: Which city, as Pliny writes to Trajan, had wastefully spent a great sum of money on unfinished aqueducts?
pairs.derivation: Building-project fact: the Nicomedians twice spent large sums on aqueducts that were left unfinished and even pulled down; Pliny asks Trajan for an engineer to finish the work (10.37-38). Entity-anchored to Nicomedia, a major city of the province; short place answer supported by the source.
